events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_partial $6.74 (model confidence 0.88)
events.body:
This is a RydeTAXI metered trip (F7), so extra distance driven flows directly into the fare and any unexcused deviation is refundable in mileage terms [RD-2]. Two off-route segments exist, F3 (18:40–18:45, +3.17 km) [F3] and F4 (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) [F4]; each is reviewed for exemption under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1].

Segment F3: at 18:37 the driver named the corridor before leaving the optimal route — "go round via Kranji Expressway?" [F8] — and the rider agreed at 18:38 [F9], both timestamps preceding the segment's 18:40 start [F3]. The rider's complaint itself concedes this: "I agreed to go round the jam near the start." Under RD-5 the consent covers the named KJE corridor, so the 3.17 km of F3 is exempt in full and no deviation finding attaches to it [RD-5].

Segment F4: the second off-route segment, 18:59–19:08, +4.78 km [F4], is a different excursion the driver never named in advance; the driver only says "the second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" [F10], which is not a rider-facing agreement [RD-5]. No consent message precedes 18:59 [F9][F4]. The driver's "reasonable cause" defence also fails: RD-4 requires a qualifying incident (accident/roadwork/breakdown/road block/heavy traffic) on the replaced stretch, and there is none — "No traffic incidents recorded near the route during the trip window" [F13] — and a speed-band record alone cannot exempt [F11][F12][RD-4]. Traffic was merely bands 5 and 4 (40–49 and 30–39 km/h) [F11][F12], not the band 1/2 condition, and the driver's own statement attributes the deviation to GPS rerouting, not to a road closure [F10][RD-4]. Nor is this a rider-named stop [RD-3], and no rider stop request preceded it [F9]. F4 is therefore an unexempted off-route segment.

Amount: only F4's extra kilometres are refundable. $1.41/km rate taken from the fare data ($40.96 ÷ 29.1 km) [F7][RD-2], applied to F4: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.7398 → $6.74 [F4][F7][RD-2]. F3's 3.17 km being exempt, it is not counted.

RD-6 does not apply: the driver's profile shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0 [F16], so this is not a "repeated" route breach and no account flag is warranted [RD-6]. Under NS-7 any refund issues as a Ryde voucher and Ryde retains final discretion [NS-7].

ruling.recommended_action: Refund $6.74 (Ryde voucher) to the rider for the non-exempt off-route segment F4 (4.78 km × $1.41/km); no account action against the driver.

What decided it: your trip was metered, so extra distance drove up your fare. One detour early in the trip was covered — the driver named the route and you agreed to it — so no refund applies there. A second detour later in the trip was not agreed to in advance, and no accident, roadwork, breakdown, road block or heavy traffic was recorded on the stretch it replaced, so those extra 4.78 km are refundable.

The $6.74 is based on your trip's rate and is paid as a Ryde voucher. Nothing else is required from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed the fare dispute on this trip and have refunded $6.74 to the rider as a Ryde voucher.

What decided it: your trip was metered, so extra distance drove up the fare. The first detour was fine — you named the route beforehand and the rider agreed. The second detour was not agreed to in advance, and no accident, roadwork, breakdown, road block or heavy traffic was recorded on the stretch it replaced, so those extra 4.78 km could not be excused. GPS rerouting alone does not exempt a detour.

No action is being taken against your account. Nothing else is required from you.
